trigger: Security noticed an unfamiliar app reading patient records through the EMR's FHIR API, launched by cardiology users at H17.

why: The report describes an unfamiliar app accessing patient records through FHIR, so check estate-wide findings for unregistered SMART on FHIR apps.
The D14 finding identifies cardiorisk.example.com as the unregistered app; trace its group, users, API, and patient-data access path.
The app path establishes the app, FHIR API, and EMR database involved; identify the observed resolver to act on the suspicious access.
Before escalating the confirmed unregistered-app finding, check prior investigation memory for approval or rejected explanations.
D14 confirms an unregistered app made 18,928 calls over 8 days to emr-fhir-api and emr-db-01; EMR application owners should investigate and contain access urgently.
